findings.claim: Fresh-process checkpoint recovery lacks a required atomic, single-consumer resume claim, allowing two shared runtimes to reconstruct and execute the same continuation.
findings.evidence: Change 06 requires: “Persist a complete owner-bound resume envelope atomically with the checkpoint and load it before live-manager lookup,” but specifies no atomic claim or competing-resume test. Its acceptance exercises only launching “a new manager.” Change 07 claims approved continuations once, while change 11 addresses team-owner exclusion; neither explicitly covers ordinary checkpoint continuations resumed concurrently through the checkpoint API. The shared profile requires “At least two runtime processes using the same durable networked SurrealDB.”
findings.suggested_fix: Require a durable CAS-based claim bound to checkpoint revision, run identity and executor incarnation before any resumed execution. Define how it interoperates with existing team ownership and supervisor exclusion without rebuilding those mechanisms. Add a production-boundary test racing two authenticated resume requests on separate runtimes, proving only one continuation can execute and that an uncertain predecessor cannot be replayed.

findings.claim: The scheduling and quiet-hours contracts leave calendar expression and timezone semantics undefined, so implementation and acceptance can disagree while satisfying the written plan.
findings.evidence: The product defaults specify “recurring IANA-zone schedules” and “Quiet hours defer delivery until the next permitted instant,” while change 14 calls for “recurring calendar schedules, IANA timezone.” No accepted recurrence grammar, supported calendar fields, timezone-change behavior, or quiet-hours timezone and interval-boundary rules are defined. Excluding “arbitrary RRULE compatibility” does not establish which recurrence expressions are supported.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the first-release recurrence input schema and supported forms, including validation and timezone revision behavior. Define quiet-hours timezone, inclusive/exclusive boundaries, overnight intervals and DST behavior. Add concrete acceptance examples to the relevant OpenSpec deltas before implementing the timing adapter and delivery policy.
